name: Batfolk
body:
Batfolk, also known as natfleers, are cave-dwelling, halfling-sized humanoids with batlike features.

Physical

Batfolk have large ears with complex structures, and their faces have several secondary ridges that provide additional sonic sensory capabilities. This all combines to provide them with fine-tuned auditory perception and combines with their darkvision to give them almost complete situational awareness within 60 feet. While their hairy faces, upturned noses, and fanged mouths make them quite frightening to behold, most are actually quite shy and gentle creatures.

Batfolk typically have gray, black, or brown fur, and small red eyes. They prefer simple, light clothing, which they make themselves from silk or special mushroom fibers.

Social

Batfolk are nocturnal by nature—although adventurers adjust their sleep patterns . While they live in underground caverns, they come out at night to forage and hunt. They are highly social, and live in communities ranging from several to several hundred families. Some of these enclaves are quite well developed, with all of the amenities of a small city.

Batfolk tend to avoid other species—more out of caution than xenophobia. Most subsist on a diet of fruit and insects, but rumors persist that they are in league with vampires, werebats, and demons, and they thus try to remain hidden and avoid confrontation.

Alignment and Religion

Most batfolk are Chaotic, but far more are Good than Evil. While they are generally benevolent, they do wish to be left alone.

Only rarely will batfolk embrace the evils that people usually associate with bats—but those who do so have been described as particularly vile and loathsome indeed.

Batfolk worship their own small pantheon, including saints of the night, the moon, the hunt, and the cave.

Names

Some typical batfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Aesarnik
Ankliara
Eskistara
Flerskin
Forstilig
Grodder
Hundinar
Jegdallen
Ompfembina
Orentar
Svannat
Upfammarask
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are agile and perceptive, but weak and off-putting. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Str, –2 Cha [standard, penalty]. (–1) Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Undercommon. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aklo, Draconic, Dwarven, Goblin, and Orc. (0)
Other Traits
Bite You have a bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d3 points of damage. (2)
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Echolocation You have impressive hearing, providing you with blindsense to a range of 60 feet. Opponents still have total concealment against you unless you can actually see them. This is a sound-dependent ability and is negated if you cannot hear, such as if you are deafened or under the effect of a silence spell. (6)
Flight (Ex) Your arms double as wings, allowing you to fly with a speed of 40 feet (poor maneuverability). You cannot fly while wearing medium or heavy armor, or while carrying a heavy load. (6)
Light Sensitivity You are dazzled while in areas of bright light (such as sunlight or a daylight spell), taking a –1 penalty on attack rolls and on visual Perception checks. (–1)
Nocturnal Knowledge (dungeoneering) and Stealth are always class skills for you. (1)
Sonic Vulnerability You take half again as much damage (+50%) from any attack that deals sonic damage. (–2)
Total: 13 RP (Advanced)
Variants
Blind Batfolk

You come from a line of batfolk who long ago stopped relying on sight entirely, and now use their echolocation exclusively to interact with the world.

Improved Echolocation You are completely blind and cannot see in the visible spectrum, but your echolocation provides you with sound-based blindsight with a range of 90 feet. You are never subject to any effect that requires you to see a target or effect, including gaze attacks and sight-based illusion effects. You can sense all foes within 90 feet as a sighted creature would. You usually do not need to make Perception checks to notice creatures within range of your blindsight. Your blindsight works perfectly in darkness of any kind, including that created by deeper darkness. Beyond that range, you treat all targets as having total concealment. Note that you are naturally sightless, so your blinded condition can only be removed by effects that grant sight to creatures with no natural vision. This trait replaces darkvision, echolocation, and light blindness.
Deep Batfolk

Long ago your ancestors abandoned the surface world entirely, retreating to the deepest recesses of Subterranea.

Deep-Dweller Your wings are suitable for gliding, and provide you with a permanent non-magical feather fall effect if you fall, but can no longer provide true flight. You gain a climb speed of 20 feet and two claw attacks that deal 1d3 damage each. This trait replaces flight.
Improved Darkvision Your darkvision extends to 120 feet, but you have the light blindness drawback instead of light sensitivity. This trait alters darkvision and replaces light sensitivity.
Oversized Batfolk

Some batfolk clans have evolved to be much larger than most of their kind. Due to their greater caloric needs, they eat larger animals and regularly hunt for game or raise livestock.

Glider Because of your larger size, your wings are unable to support you in flight. However, you can glide on them, and they provide you with a permanent, non-magical feather fall effect. Your base land speed is 30 feet, and you gain a +2 species bonus to Acrobatics checks. This trait replaces flight.

Oversized You are size Medium, and your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Wis, –4 Cha. This trait alters size and ability score modifiers.
Alternate Species Traits
Batspeech You can use speak with animals as a constant spell-like ability, but only to speak with bats, including giant bats and other bat-like animals. This trait replaces nocturnal.
Blood Drinker Unlike most batfolk, you subsist mostly on a diet of blood, like a vampire bat. When you deal damage to a living creature with your bite attack, you gain 1 temporary hit point by ingesting the target’s blood. This ability does not work on creatures that do not have blood. This trait replaces darkvision.
Septic Bite Your diet includes carrion and trash, and makes your mouth home to dangerous bacteria. A number of times per day equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1), when you deal damage to a creature with your bite attack, you can inject your septic saliva into the wound as a swift action. This trait replaces nocturnal.
Septic Saliva—disease (injury); save Fortitude DC 10 + 1/2 your Hit Dice + your Constitution modifier; onset immediate; frequency 1/day; effect staggered for 1 round (initial effect) then 1d3 Dex (continuing effect); cure 1 save.
Screech Once per day you can use lesser confusion as a spell-like ability, but this requires a vocal component. You use your character level as the caster level, and Charisma as your casting ability. This trait replaces nocturnal.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1/2 to the number of bombs per day you can create.
Cleric Add a +1 bonus on caster level checks made to overcome the spell resistance of aberrations.
Fighter Add +1 to the fighter’s CMD when resisting a drag or grapple attempt.
Monk Add +1/4 point to your ki pool.
Ranger Add a +1/2 bonus on wild empathy checks to influence animals and magical beasts that live underground.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Stealth checks and Perception checks made in dim light or darkness.
Sorcerer Add +1/2 point of damage to sorcerer spells you cast that have the shadow descriptor.
Vigilante Add +1/2 to the DC increase from unshakable.
Witch Add +1/4 to your caster level when determining the effects of the spells granted to you by your patron.
